Both link forms have been confirmed usable. The raw.githubusercontent.com link was actually fetched, returned 200, and the byte count matched the catalogue exactly. The via CDN link could not be checked in the environment that generated this page — access to cdn.jsdelivr.net is prohibited there — so it was constructed according to the URL form specified in the jsDelivr documentation, and the owner manually tried one of them on 2026-09-20. Both are kept: one is provided at zero cost to this project, and a reader who finds one of them unusable can still use the other.

Included replica — not the WHO website, and not live content. This page was generated by {folioAssistant} from its own {iris} catalogue, which is modelled by reference: {figures}. The WHO logo is deliberately omitted, and the generated covers are not displayed for the same reason — the covers carry the emblem printed on the publication.
Included replica. Generated by {generator} from {catalogue}. The layout follows {iris}; every number on this page is read from the catalogue, not copied from a screenshot.

No Dublin Core record. The catalogue states this truthfully rather than synthesizing metadata from the PDF — this is rule R8 of the iris-dspace skill: when a record exists, never infer metadata from the PDF; its converse is that a missing record remains missing.

This is an entry page, not the library visualization tool. The full library/ visualization tool is task jbx2, being built separately. This page imitates the IRIS home page and links to other pages, rather than becoming a second answer to the same problem.

One item, three routes — this is exactly the point. The catalogue records this item only once; the bytes can be obtained at WHO upstream, at the replica page here, and from a CDN edge node — jsDelivr serves any public repository, so the last route brings no hosting cost to this project. The knowledge graph states what exists and where; the CDN states nothing, it is only responsible for serving the files.

Where the kept copies actually are — task yl5w. The catalogue records each of them at uploads/<name>.pdf relative to who-iris/, and all three of these paths are missing: #477 moved library/ into this instance but left uploads/ in cat-harness/.
The cover has been generated and kept here, but not published: {gates}.
A cover has been generated and recorded for this item, but is not displayed: the publication's cover bears the WHO emblem, and this replica is not published in WHO's name.

Each row provides three routes to the same item: the IRIS source at WHO upstream, this repository's own local replica page, and the resource itself — downloadable from the repository, or alternatively from a CDN edge node.

Every row below is usable. When this repository does not keep a row, that row is not shown greyed out but is marked {referenced}; this is the actual state, and is exactly the meaning of a catalogue modelled by reference. {materialized} means the bytes are right here.

The download links above point to where the bytes actually are, so they are usable. What is wrong is the declaration in the catalogue, and check:catalogue does not check localPath at all — it only verifies metadataRef and libraryId, and reports a pass for three materialized declarations that point to nowhere.
The interface is displayed in {language}. Publication titles, authors, abstracts and other catalogue records are all displayed exactly as published by WHO.

The primary objective of the Institutional Repository for Information Sharing (IRIS) is to provide free digital access to the scientific and technical publications of the World Health Organization (WHO), including the outputs of its country offices, regional offices and headquarters. In addition, IRIS also covers the mandates established by the Organization's governing bodies in cooperation with its Member States.
